# task-03696608: three-color edge-ray extension

## Rule supported by two demos and one solved test
A 3-cell horizontal seed [A,B,C] extends vertical rays in each seed column. Other isolated markers matching A, B, or C are endpoints/anchors for horizontal rays extending from their column to the corresponding edge. The rays meet and include the marker cells, and all unrelated cells stay unchanged.

Vertical ray lengths are determined as follows in observed examples: A's vertical ray ends at the row of the isolated A marker on the left edge; C's vertical ray ends at the row of the isolated C marker on the right edge; B's vertical ray ends at the row of its isolated B marker when present, otherwise continues to the bottom edge. Do not blindly extend all three columns to the boundary: the first test attempt was wrong because the A and C rays continued past their respective side-marker rows. If a marker is absent, use demos and test layout to infer that ray's endpoint; only B's absent-marker case has been observed to continue to the bottom.

## Evidence
- Demo 1 (15×15): seed row 0, columns 5–7 = [6,5,3]. Side markers: 6 at (4,0), 3 at (2,14). Extend vertical 6 in col5 through row4; 5 in col6 through row14; 3 in col7 through row2. Extend horizontal 6 from left marker across row4 through col5; 3 from right marker across row2 through col7.
- Demo 2 (12×12): seed row 0, columns 4–6 = [5,3,8]. Markers: 5 at (4,0), 3 at (8,0), 8 at (5,11). Extend vertical 5 col4 through row4, 3 col5 through row8, 8 col6 through row5. Extend horizontals from each marker to its seed column and edge.
- Solved test (11×11): seed [4,8,5] at row0 cols3–5; markers 4 at (7,0), 5 at (9,10), no additional 8 marker. Correct vertical 4 col3 through row7 and 5 col5 through row9, with 8 col4 through row10; horizontal 4 across row7 cols0–3, and 5 across row9 cols5–10. The mistaken output extended 4 through rows8–9 and 5 through row10."
